When it gets "stuck" at 33%, that is the step were files are being scanned, their paths being shown in the dialog. Does the path not change after a while in your end? If so, could you upload the files that are getting stuck?

Depending on the quantity of files and their size, that can take a while, especially in the first scan, when the results aren't cached yet.

Well I cannot share the file it gets stuck at, 
it's a file with +6K lines of code, the logic core of the app I got published on Google Store..

-When I tried Beta4, I left the thing there for 5 minutes or smth, 
and everything seemed to be idling, no hdd activity, cpu was quiet..

I will try it again and report,
maybe on the next beta it can get to the end..

-However on version 4.4.1 stable,
the process of scanning the same exact File and project (with many other ,gd .cs and .tscn files..) was >> Instantaneous.

I could not even see the Progress Bar window appear, it just did it on the fly.

At least we know Beta4 is trying tho!

> it's a file with +6K lines of code, the logic core of the app I got published on Google Store.

Yeah, that definitely will take some time to scan. I would recommend dividing that script in smaller chunks, not just because of this, but because it's not good practice to have massive script files if it can be helped.

> -However on version 4.4.1 stable,
the process of scanning the same exact File and project (with many other ,gd .cs and .tscn files..) was >> Instantaneous.

That's likely because the results of said file were already cached, and so not re-scanned until it was modified again.

---

By the way, the reason the "Cancel" button doesn't work is because the main thread is busy with the scanning. It isn't noticeable with various small files, but is with larger ones. The ideal would be making the scanning happen in a thread, but that's a different issue.

Ok!
I have tried the "Detect from Project" feature in the new Godot 4.5 beta5, and I can confirm:
The Feature works Perfectly. 

Even tho the Progress Bar was stuck for 30 minutes, it managed to parse the full file/project,
and then the list updated disabling the unnecessary elements.. excellent!

Case closed!

-The only thing that could be considered is the speed/time it takes..

In 4.4.1 stable the process was Instantaneous.
In 4.5beta5 it took 30 minutes, so there's a difference..

But ofc, as long as it can Complete the process it's all good,
and it's a considerably complex (although small) project.



-Besides the only other thing that stood out would be:
With beta5 I'm getting tis Error lots of times on init:
ERROR: Condition "index < 0 || index >= t.length()" is true. Continuing.
   at: accessibility_create_sub_text_edit_elements (drivers/accesskit/accessibility_driver_accesskit.cpp:380)

And a couple other uid file warns which I guess,
should be a matter of reimporting or taking care of those asset files..

I will still need to refactor a few things on the app code, and java plugin code too,
but so far so good!

-Also Glad to see it still works on my ancient AMD FX8350, 
which has SSE 4.2 and AVX, but not AVX2.. I kno it's super old at this point, but it still works like a charm!

If there's a list of "keep using AVX1 and not AVX2 until strictly necessary" users, count me in! :D

> In 4.4.1 stable the process was Instantaneous.
In 4.5beta5 it took 30 minutes, so there's a difference..

In 4.4.*, scripts weren't scanned at all.

Given the core concern of "Detect from Project" being non-functional is now addressed, I'll go ahead and close this. Speed can be tracked in a separate issue if desired; however, given that the previous behavior was literally no scanning whatsoever, we're probably inherently limited in addressing that

Since the old process was Instantaneous,
and the new implementation can take considerable time.. 0sec vs +30min on my small project..

Perhaps it would make sense having a way to Store the "Engine Compilation Configuration Profile", 
so that the next time you start Godot and load the project, you don't need to repeat the entire process again.. right?
The profile can already be saved and loaded. Also, the results are cached, and files are only rescanned when modified.

My bad, I completely missed/forgot about that.. lol

Fact of the matter is, in dev3:
"Detect from Project" - Works!
"Save Profile" - Works! And generates a .gdbuild file
"Load Profile" does not work.. it does nothing, even tho I generated the .gdbuild file with that very same project.

Then I don't know if it's the expected behavior but,
When Restarting Godot, and opening the same exact project where the "Detect from Project" process completed,
the "Configuration Profile" is not preserved/restored.. it's Reseted

So I have to do the Detection process again.

-Then alas it's apparently all for nothing because:
Even tho the resulting final "Detected Profile" has many many elements Deselected like: 
3D Engine, 3D Physics, XR, Navigation, and a LOT of node types..

The Android export generates an AAB file of the Same Size, apparently ignoring the Profile,
whether 100% of the elements are included on final build, or not.

-I would try to do it with beta5, 
but it breaks my Android app in too many fronts, so I cannot even run it.

In dev4 to beta3 some little things broke like,
some popup menus (solved)
a custom Google Play Integrity Java Plugin (probably solvable as I was indicated)

And that's allright, some adjustments are expected in big refactors like this..

But beta5 also rejects the .ttf fonts that work Perfectly on previous versions,
and work perfectly on my app built with dev3.

Just normal ttf fonts, or rather, a Subset I made with "pyftsubset" of some fonts like:
Notosans, Carlito, Tinos, Fahkwang, WenQuanYiZenHei..

Since the app refuses to run with beta5 and breaks the fonts too,
I can only wait for next beta6, or for a more Final Stable version... 

Then I will address all the problems and correct the code, or whatever needs to be corrected.

Meanwhile I'm using dev3 with a very Updated Android Export Template, 
the full android dependency chain update worked Perfectly and trouble free.. (which was quite amazing..)

And now I'm trying to fix the 16KB memory alignment problem for the Mono part of the build..
It should be a matter of Compressing the libraries on Export, but somehow Godot manages to bypass all my edits on the Templates, be it on the Scons side, Gradle side, or even Manifest stuff.

Ok I have testesd it with Beta5..

In beta5:
"Detect from Project" - Works!
"Save Profile" - Works! And generates a .gdbuild file
"Load Profile" - Works! and correctly recalls the configuration from the .gdbuild file.

Then Configuration Profile is correctly Restored when restarting Godot.
Excellent!

-What I'm still not seeing tho is Size reduction..
So the Android export generates an AAB file of the Same Size, apparently ignoring the Profile,
whether 100% of the elements are included on final build, or not.


-What's more..
For whatever reason now my app built correctly, seems to work perfectly on my Android11 Phone!

I already adressed the Popup problems on the code..

But the Problems with the custom Google Play Integrity Java Plugin, 
and the custom Fonts have dissapeared.. gone!

It's quite Baffling, app is the same, all caches were cleared before.. so I dont lknow,
but positive indeed!

OK, I've been able to test the Size Reduction matter..

The behavior remains, and the outcome is the same:
With Beta5 Android Export generates an AAB file of the Same Size, apparently ignoring the Profile.

Process:
Completely cleared all Caches, including .godot, home/cache/godot and home/.gradle,
installed a fresh Template and placed the manifest..

First I exported a build with the "Engine Compilation Configuration Profile" untouched, all elements Enabled:
FullEngine.aab > 126.5 MiB (132,610,946)

Then I did the "Detect from Project" proces, and it correctly identified and selected the proper elements/nodes.

Then I saved the Profile which I'm sharing here..

Finally I exported a second build with the actual Profile, and all the unnecessary elements Disabled:
Profile.aab > 126.5 MiB (132,610,944)

-Since that's not right, I deleted the Android Template, cleared the home/.gradle folder again, 
installed a new Template, and made another export build with the actual Profile confirmed, the unnecessary elements Disabled:

Profile2.aab > 126.5 MiB (132,610,918)

-So I'd say it's pretty much confirmed!
There's some heavy elements deselected like the entire 3D Engine, 3D Physics, XR and Navigation..
so the difference cannot be bit sized..

Can you guys replicate this on your end?

-Meanwhile I'm gonna try compiling custom Templates with all the unnecessary elements removed..
Let's see how that goes!

[ECProfileb5.gdbuild.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21824371/ECProfileb5.gdbuild.txt)
I'm sorry if this comes out as a stupid question but, you _are_ **recompiling** the Android preset used for exporting using the generated profile file, right?

Recompiling what?
the Android Export preset? 
how do you recompile that? ...

If you mean recompiling the Android Template via Scons.. 
that's what I began doing yesterday as a last resource, and to great results I might add..!

-It's probably my fault, but..
the fact I though the "Engine Compilation Configuration Profile" and the Scons Template building process were Separate methods one could use to Reduce build size... and not One and part of the Same, shows > the documentation, or the way the "Engine Compilation Configuration Profile" is presented to the user on the UI, doesn't give the user the appropriate information/feedback.

-I thought "Engine Compilation Configuration Profile" was a Separate feature that made Godot export the builds in a customized manner.

Nowhere it's indicated that the generated "Engine Compilation Configuration Profile" is Only to be used with Scons for Template generation.

So the natural thing to assume is > Godot will use that Profile to make a custom Export, 
not including the Deselected elements on Build, and thus making a smaller build.

That's what I assumed,
and what probably most new users will assume when looking at the "Engine Compilation Configuration Profile" window.

It will make all the sense, and there's also ways to do it this way no?
there's actual methods to exclude elements on export, right?

-And that's a bit of the problem..
By looking at the window what makes sense is assuming this will include/exclude elements on Export.

It's only by knowing considerably more about Godot's backend that one can deduce the whole "Engine Compilation Configuration Profile" is just a tool for Scons Template generation!


-So yeah.. in essence the "Engine Compilation Configuration Profile" and features are working Perfectly.. 

But perhaps it needs to present the info in a clearer way?
